root_cause.text: MPTCP's mptcp_subflow_init() copies the tcpv6_prot structure (including its NULL slab pointer) into tcpv6_prot_override before TCPv6's slab cache is registered via proto_register, causing MPTCP v6 subflow sockets to be allocated from a non-RCU-safe kmalloc cache and leading to a slab-use-after-free during concurrent ehash lookups.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states: "MPTCP's mptcp_subflow_init() copies tcpv6_prot into tcpv6_prot_override during inet_init() ... before inet6_init() has called proto_register(&tcpv6_prot). At that point, tcpv6_prot.slab is still NULL, so tcpv6_prot_override.slab remains NULL permanently." The patch fixes this by moving the IPv6-specific initialization into a new function called later, after proto_register has executed.

candidates.rationale: This explicitly sets the slab cache pointer to NULL for the MPTCPv6 protocol structure, leading to non-RCU-safe kmalloc allocations for MPTCP subflow sockets.
This copies the entire mptcp_prot structure (including its possibly NULL or unregistered slab pointer) into mptcp_v6_prot, contributing to the use of an invalid slab.
Setting psock_update_sk_prot to NULL is part of the initialization pattern, but the underlying slab pointer may already be NULL due to premature copy of tcpv6_prot.

This line initializes the MPTCP v6 subflow protocol override, but the struct copy (including NULL slab) likely occurs earlier in the function, causing future socket allocations to bypass the RCU-safe slab cache.
This declaration of mptcp_proto_v6_init() is critical because its execution order relative to mptcp_subflow_init() determines whether the slab cache is registered before the structure copy.

vuln_statements.explanation: This explicitly sets the slab cache pointer to NULL for the MPTCPv6 protocol structure, causing MPTCP v6 sockets to be allocated from kmalloc instead of a registered RCU-safe slab cache, leading to use-after-free during concurrent ehash lookups.

This copies the entire mptcp_prot structure (including its possibly NULL slab pointer) into mptcp_v6_prot, propagating the invalid slab configuration that results in non-RCU-safe allocations for MPTCP subflow sockets.

This line is part of the initialization of the TCPv6 protocol override for MPTCP subflows; the copy of the entire tcpv6_prot structure (including its NULL slab) occurs earlier in mptcp_subflow_init(), so this line contributes to the setup that leads to allocation from a non-RCU-safe cache and the subsequent use-after-free.

Similar to the IPv6 case, this line initializes the IPv4 protocol override as part of the same mptcp_subflow_init() function; while the root cause focuses on v6, this pattern also copies an unregistered slab pointer for TCPv4, potentially causing a similar issue for IPv4 subflow sockets.

This declaration is critical because the execution order of mptcp_proto_v6_init (which registers the TCPv6 slab cache via proto_register) relative to mptcp_subflow_init (which copies the tcpv6_prot structure) determines whether the slab pointer is valid. If mptcp_subflow_init runs before the slab is registered, the NULL slab is copied, causing the vulnerability.
